provisions.summary: Hawaiian home general loan fund also receives moneys under HRS 237D-2(f) (transient accommodations tax revenue deposits). Appropriation/fund-routing provision, not an income tax item.
provisions.quote: moneys received pursuant to section 237D-2(f), Hawaii Revised Statutes

provisions.summary: Raises the transient accommodations tax rate by 1 percentage point (to 10.25% from 9.25%) for periods beginning January 1, 2026, on transient accommodations and resort time share units; the added revenue goes to the Hawaiian home general loan fund. This is a transient accommodations tax change, which the income tax spec cannot express.
provisions.quote: 10.25 per cent for the period beginning on January 1, 2026, and thereafter

provisions.summary: Deposits the revenue above what the lower rates would have raised quarterly into the Hawaiian home general loan fund. This is fund earmarking, not an income tax item.
provisions.quote: shall be deposited quarterly into the Hawaiian home general loan fund established pursuant to section 213

provisions.summary: Excludes the section 237D-2(f) revenues from the priority distribution under 237D-6.5(b), so the new revenue bypasses the convention center, Turtle Bay, tourism emergency and land funds. Fund allocation only.
provisions.quote: Except for the revenues collected pursuant to section 237D-2(e)[,] and (f)

notes: No income tax, credit or deduction provision, so the spec is null. The bill changes only the transient accommodations tax (HRS 237D) and fund routing, which belong on the state-taxes path (`python -m fiscal_notes state-run`), not the income tax spec. Two things for a reviewer: (1) The 1 percentage point increase is written as a step to 10.25% from 1/1/2026, but the bill leaves the existing 1-point surcharge in 237D-2(e) (to the mass transit fund, through 12/31/2030) in place, so the combined rate during that window is 11.25%, not 10.25%. The 10.25% base figure in (a)(6) and (c)(4) is the new rate before the (e) surcharge. (2) The January 1, 2026 start date is already past as of this session, and Section 6 takes effect upon approval, so the retroactivity of the first months is a question for a reviewer. Sections 4 to 6 are saving, drafting and effective-date boilerplate and are not listed as provisions.
